text:
Presbyterian College women's tennis earns ITA Team Academic Award for third straight year
Seven Presbyterian College women's tennis players were named 2026 Intercollegiate Tennis Association (ITA) Scholar-Athletes, according to a July 15 announcement from the college.
The Blue Hose team received the All-Academic Team award after posting a cumulative grade point average of 3.63 during the 2025-26 academic year, surpassing the ITA's minimum requirement of a 3.20 GPA. This marks the third consecutive year and tenth overall time that Presbyterian has earned this distinction as a team.
Ladina Bruhin, Sofia Rodrigo Hidalgo, Roxy Valdes, Katherine Bauer, Mary Ellen Longmire, Elle Sceney, and McKenzie Davis were all recognized as ITA Scholar-Athletes. For Bruhin, Rodrigo Hidalgo, Valdes, Bauer, and Sceney, it was their first time receiving this honor. Longmire earned her second straight award, while Davis achieved her fourth career recognition. Davis is now only the second player in program history to be named an ITA Scholar-Athlete four times.
On-court achievements accompanied these academic honors. Bruhin and Valdes led the team in spring competition by earning All-Big South honors and excelling in doubles play to secure spots on the All-Conference Doubles Second Team. In singles matches, Bruhin and Longmire each recorded nine wins; Bruhin was named to the All-Conference Singles Second Team, while Longmire secured a place on the league's All-Academic Team.
During fall competition, Bruhin and Davis won the Big South Doubles Championship, which granted them automatic entry into the ITA Conference Masters Championships in San Diego, where they reached the round of sixteen.
To qualify as an ITA Scholar-Athlete, a player must be a varsity letter winner with at least a 3.50 GPA for that academic year and have been enrolled at their current school for at least two semesters.
